concerns.text: Task T011 (Integration test for data ingestion) is listed before T013 (Ingestion script) and T012 (Descriptors). T011 explicitly states '(Requires T013 completion)'. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule; the test cannot be written/verified before the code it tests exists. T011 must follow T013.

Task T015 (Dataset capping) depends on T013 (Ingestion) and T012 (Descriptors) to have data to cap. However, T015 is listed before T012 and T013 in the task list. While T015 is logically dependent, the ordering implies T015 could be attempted before the data pipeline is built. T015 must be placed after T013 and T012.

Task T025 (Paired t-test) is listed before T026 (Bonferroni correction). The task description for T025 states: 'Apply Bonferroni correction (from T026) as the primary method'. This creates a circular dependency in the text and a logical violation in the order: the consumer (T025) precedes the producer (T026). T026 must precede T025.

Task T031 (Apply Bonferroni correction to final p-values) is listed after T025 (Paired t-test) but before T027 (Generate model_performance_metrics.json). T031 modifies the metrics that T027 generates. T031 must precede T027 to ensure the generated artifact contains the corrected values.

Task T009 and T010 are marked [P] (parallel-safe) and placed before T012 (Implementation). While TDD allows writing tests first, the [P] tag implies they can run in parallel with other tasks. However, T009 tests `features/descriptors.py` which does not exist until T012. If 'run' implies execution, this is impossible. If 'run' implies 'write', the [P] tag is misleading regarding execution. Clarify that [P] applies only to 'writing' phase or remove [P] if execution is implied.
